Q1: Ethanol has internationally recognized known hazards (Tier 1) for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive toxicity, and organ/systemic effects. Additionally, an expanded perspective (Tier 2) based on scientific literature and predictive models indicates potential environmental, endocrine disruption, inhalation, oral, and dermal/eye hazards.
Q2: Ethanol appears on lists of concern due to its classification as a Group 1 carcinogen by IARC and its identification as a potential endocrine disruptor by TEDX. However, it is also found on low hazard lists, including the SCIL Green Circle list and as a substance added to food, suggesting its low hazard status often refers to tightly regulated conditions or very low quantities.
Q3: Ethanol is exceptionally well-characterized, evidenced by an extensive scientific literature of 898,000 references and a maximum number of 925 toxicology records in the EPA ToxValDB, indicating broad study across multiple programs. Its specific molecular formula and substance class also confirm it is a well-defined chemical with no data-deficient hazard classifications.
